prerequisites: Appreciation of the quality of mechanical systems based on their characteristics.
Use of performance evaluation methods for mechanical subsystems in evaluating their operational efficiency.

learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate identifies and describes basic concepts, principles and methods from mathematics, physics, chemistry, technical drawing, economics and computer science, with application in quality assurance.

The student/graduate explains and interprets theoretical and experimental results from mathematics, physics, chemistry, economics, technical drawing and computer science, with application in quality assurance.
The student/graduate operates with basic concepts, principles and methods from mathematics, physics, chemistry, technical drawing, economics and computer science, applying them in quality assurance.

The student/graduate applies evaluation criteria and methods for identifying, modeling, experimenting, analyzing and qualitative and quantitative assessment of phenomena and processes specific to the fundamental field, including using digital technologies.
The student/graduate applies the values of ethics and deontology of the engineering profession.
The student/graduate practices logical reasoning, evaluation and self-evaluation in decision-making.
The student/graduate works efficiently as a team member or leader.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to quality management
Characteristics of product and service quality.
Forms of quality. Evolution of the quality concept. Total quality
Total Quality. Quality management system
Quality models
Quality standards from the SR EN ISO 9000 series
Excellence models in the field of quality.
Techniques and tools used in quality analysis
Classic and modern techniques and tools.
Quality in design
Product quality characteristics used in design.
Quality tools used in design.
Project quality management.
Methods used in product quality planning
Quality Function Deployment. Failure Mode and Effects Analysis. Taguchi Method.
Quality control
Elements of statistics. Production process control.
Statistical acceptance control. Dependability.
Quality evaluation
Quality audit. Conformity certification.
Methods for quality improvement
Specific methods and techniques for quality improvement.
Six Sigma. TPS Toyota. Reengineering.
Economic analysis of quality
Objectives and methods. Quality cost analysis.
Economic efficiency of quality improvement
Basic quality. Case study concepts.
Quality standards from the ISO 9000 family.
Benchmarking. Case study.
Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA). Case study.
Quality audit and conformity certification. Legislation. Case study.
Methods used in product quality design. Taguchi Method.
Methods for quality improvement. Six Sigma.
teaching_methods: Direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)
Action-based methods (exercise, practical activities, problem solving)

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory activities (completion of lab sheets, lab colloquium)

assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained from the Colloquium and Laboratory activities, each contributing 50%. Students must achieve a minimum grade of 5 for both the Colloquium (final written test) and Laboratory activities. All laboratory works must be completed, with recovery allowed for only one outstanding laboratory work. The minimum passing grade for the course is 5.
